title: Structural Silence: When AI Infrastructure Fails Speakers of Underrepresented Languages
abstract: arXiv:2608.12278v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Artificial intelligence tools for education and language support are increasingly framed as scalable responses to access gaps in under-resourced communities. Yet the infrastructure underlying these tools, including training corpora, tokenization schemes, evaluation benchmarks, and deployment architectures, can systematically disadvantage speakers of underrepresented languages before a model is trained.   This paper examines these structural barriers through Bengali, one of the world's most widely spoken languages, focusing on AI-assisted education in low-connectivity environments. translated_title: 结构性沉默：当人工智能基础设施让未被充分代表语言的说话者失效时
translated_abstract: 用于教育和语言支持的人工智能工具，日益被描述为应对资源不足社区获取差距的可扩展解决方案。然而，这些工具背后的基础设施，包括训练语料库、分词方案、评估基准和部署架构，可能在模型训练之前就系统性地使未被充分代表语言的说话者处于不利地位。本文通过孟加拉语（世界上使用最广泛的语言之一）考察这些结构性障碍，重点关注低连接环境中的AI辅助教育。我们识别出四个相互关联的失败：严重的网络存在差距——孟加拉语占全球人口近4%，却仅占全球网络内容的不到0.5%；在主要多语言语料库中，英语和孟加拉语之间的训练令牌赤字为67:1；与孟加拉语的音节文字相关的分词惩罚，这加剧了……
tldr: 本文揭示了AI基础设施中的结构性偏见如何通过训练数据、分词和部署架构，在模型训练前就系统性排斥孟加拉语等未被充分代表语言的使用者，并提出了四重相互关联的失败机制。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals how structural biases in AI infrastructure—through training data, tokenization, and deployment architectures—systematically disadvantage speakers of underrepresented languages like Bengali before model training, identifying four interlocking failure mechanisms.
